newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-BT says should not pay windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BT says should not pay windfall tax.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc denied on Thursday that it had put aside money to pay a windfall tax that the opposition Labour Party has said it would impose on cash-rich utilities if it came to power.

Finance director Robert Brace told Reuters in an interview that the group was not a utility. Neither its shareholders nor executives had seen the same extraordinary gains that Labour alleged other companies had received, and BT did not expect to have to pay up.
"I don't think it's right and proper that BT should be included in the net if there is such a tax," Brace said.
Brace noted that unlike water and electricity companies, BT had been operating in a competitive market for some time.

Some analysts have estimated that BT, which has a current gearing level of under five percent, could afford to pay between 1.0 billion stg and 1.4 billion stg in windfall tax, which Labour has said it would use to tackle youth unemployment.
Labour, which looks a likely winner at the next general election, due by next May, has said it aims to raise more than five billion stg from a windfall tax on the profits of the privatised utilities.
